data.Name: handle.name
data.Title: handle.name
data.Description:
Dot-separated hierarchical identifier composed of lowercase segments.
Each segment must begin with a lowercase alphabetic character and may
contain lowercase alphanumeric characters with optional internal
hyphen-separated words. Hierarchy is expressed from left to right,
with the most significant component appearing first.

data.Name: left.right.dot
data.Title: left.right.dot
data.Description:
Dot-separated hierarchical identifier composed of lowercase
alphanumeric segments. The first segment must begin with a
lowercase alphabetic character. Subsequent segments may begin
with either a lowercase letter or digit. Hierarchy is expressed
from left to right, with the most significant component appearing first.

data.Name: market.slot.name
data.Title: market.slot.name
data.Description:
Dot-separated identifier for a specific market slot.
The first segment identifies the market commodity class and MUST be one of `e`, `r`, or `d`. The second segment identifies the market type. The final segment is a 10-digit Unix timestamp in seconds giving the slot start. The middle segments identify the market maker alias and must satisfy the left-right-dot naming rules.
The slot start timestamp MUST align to the duration required by the market type.

data.Title: relay.open.or.closed
data.Description:
Binary state of a single-pole relay contact. Describes whether the relay 
contact is open (not conducting) or closed (conducting), regardless of 
coil energization state.

Note 1: The coil energization required to achieve a contact state depends 
on relay type:
- Normally Open (NO) relay: energized coil → closed contact
- Normally Closed (NC) relay: de-energized coil → closed contact

Note 2: This enum is specifically for single-pole relays with binary states.
Other relay configurations (double-throw, multi-position, latching, etc.) 
require different state enumerations that capture their specific switching 
patterns.

Tight mode keeps the buffer within a narrowly regulated temperature band, permitting frequent charge and discharge transitions to maintain relatively constant buffer energy. Heat pump short-cycling is prevented by alternating between charging the buffer and the store.

data.Title: analytics.channel.gt
data.Description:
Canonical definition of a computed telemetry channel scoped to a single terminal asset and produced outside SCADA systems.
An analytics.channel.gt declares a computation over message streams, telemetry, or system behavior associated with a specific terminal asset. These channels represent analytics-derived signals such as persistence delay, heartbeat-based health, or other observational metrics.
Unlike derived.channel.gt, analytics.channel.gt is not computed by a GridWorks GNode. Its semantic authority lies in external analytics systems.
data.RawJson: {"x-gridworks-extended_description": "`analytics.channel.gt` defines computed telemetry channels whose semantic authority lies outside SCADA systems and whose scope is a single terminal asset.\nValues associated with `analytics.channel.gt` SHALL be represented as floating point numbers, with the unit defined by OutputUnit.\nMulti-terminal-asset computations (e.g. aggregation across assets or GNode-based selection) are intentionally excluded from this type and should be represented by a separate aggregation type."}

data.Title: bid
data.Description:
A market-normalized, slot-specific price–quantity schedule submitted by a market participant. A bid expresses willingness to inject or withdraw a quantity of a market-defined commodity as a function of price, subject to the rules of the MarketType associated with the specified MarketSlot.
Bids are economically admissible, cryptographically anchored messages that serve as the primary input to market aggregation and clearing. Differences between participant classes (e.g. leaf nodes, aggregators, fleets, generators) are expressed through MarketType rules and bidder authorization registries, not through differences in bid structure.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "The bid type is the foundational economic message of the GridWorks market architecture. By enforcing strict normalization against MarketType-defined price and quantity domains, bids enable a self-scaling market maker strategy in which aggregation, clearing, and dispatch logic can be applied uniformly across participant classes and market layers.
All bids share a common structure and validation contract. Differences in physical assets, aggregation scope, or operational responsibility are expressed through external registries, MarketType definitions, and settlement processes rather than through specialized bid schemas.
This design supports permissioned or permissionless participation, economic rate-limiting via fees, and bounded computational complexity, while preserving extensibility for future market products and clearing mechanisms.
"}

data.Title: channel.config
data.Description: Base channel configuration used by component definitions to describe how a telemetry channel is sampled, scaled, and serialized.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "`channel.config` captures both periodic sampling behavior and optional asynchronous emission behavior for a telemetry channel.
`PollPeriodMs` and `CapturePeriodS` describe different stages of SCADA behavior. `PollPeriodMs` is the cadence at which SCADA polls the hardware device or upstream source for a value. `CapturePeriodS` is the cadence at which SCADA emits that channel value into the telemetry stream.
These cadences may differ. For example, SCADA may poll a device frequently to maintain fresh local state while only reporting the value periodically or when an async trigger condition is met.
In current runtime practice, `AsyncCapture` may be true even when `AsyncCaptureDelta` is omitted. This means asynchronous capture is enabled, but the threshold semantics are not fully specified in the payload itself.
When `AsyncCaptureDelta` is present, the intended interpretation is: publish asynchronously when the magnitude of the change since the last published value is greater than or equal to `AsyncCaptureDelta`.
`Exponent` describes how to interpret the serialized integer reading relative to `Unit`. For example, if `Unit` is `Gpm` and `Exponent` is `2`, then a reading value of `432` represents `4.32 Gpm`.
A future published version may strengthen this contract by requiring `AsyncCaptureDelta` whenever `AsyncCapture` is true, once runtime behavior consistently provides that value.
"}

data.Title: connectivity.edge.gt
data.Description:
Directed topological edge connecting two Grid Nodes (GNodes) in the physical electric network. This type encodes copper-level adjacency used for graph-based modeling, Kirchhoff power flow calculations, and constraint propagation.
A ConnectivityEdge represents an oriented structural relationship between two distinct GNodes. Direction SHALL be interpreted as the positive reference direction for flow modeling and graph traversal. Physical power MAY flow in either direction subject to system conditions.
For a given pair of GNodes, only one structural ConnectivityEdge SHALL exist. Reverse flow SHALL be represented by sign conventions in power quantities and SHALL NOT be modeled by introducing a secondConnectivityEdge reversing the same GNode pair.
ConnectivityEdge does not encode electrical impedance, capacity, or switching state. It defines structural topology only.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "ConnectivityEdge represents structural conductor adjacency only. Most edges correspond directly to parent–child relationships in the GNode hierarchy (for example, substation to feeder or feeder to downstream connectivity node). In these cases, the directed edge makes explicit the physical copper relationship already implied by the structural topology.
However, real distribution systems may contain tie-lines, loops, and alternate routing paths. The graph formed by ConnectivityEdge objects MAY therefore contain cycles. Acyclicity is not assumed.
The directed orientation of a ConnectivityEdge establishes a positive reference direction for flow modeling and graph traversal. It does NOT restrict physical power flow to a single direction. Reverse flow SHALL be represented by sign conventions in power quantities rather than by duplicating edges in the opposite direction.
Status expresses lifecycle participation of the edge in the registry and coordination system. It SHALL NOT be interpreted as operational switching state (e.g., breaker open or closed). Operational configuration of the active network graph MUST be modeled using separate types designed for dynamic topology state.
Conceptually, ConnectivityEdge aligns with the conductor adjacency relationships represented in IEC 61970/61968 CIM (Common Information Model), where network topology is derived from connections between ConnectivityNodes through conducting equipment. ConnectivityEdge provides a simplified, distribution-level abstraction suitable for graph-based modeling and transactive coordination without adopting the full CIM equipment hierarchy."}

{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "Grid Nodes (GNodes) provide the stable identity layer for distributed coordination in the GridWorks ecosystem. Each GNode participates in a hierarchical alias structure that encodes topology, routing semantics, and coordination scope.
GNodes may represent physical grid structure (e.g., metered boundaries, connectivity nodes, constraint points) or logical and service roles (e.g., SCADA agents, forecasting services, market participants). BaseClass defines the universal structural ontology required for interoperability. GNodeClass expresses organization-specific functional roles and does not alter structural semantics.
`g.node.gt` is an immutable serialized snapshot of declared node state. Any change to a GNode (alias updates, status changes, relocations, or classification changes) SHALL be represented by publishing a new `g.node.gt` message rather than mutating a previously published instance. This preserves durable identity (GNodeId) while allowing controlled evolution of descriptive attributes.
GNode is designed as the atomic unit of coordination in a recursively composable grid architecture. Systems of arbitrary scale are formed by composing GNodes into hierarchical or heterarchical structures. This allows optimal power flow (OPF), market clearing, and constraint coordination mechanisms to operate centrally, regionally, or in distributed configurations without altering the underlying identity model.
Conceptually, GNode aligns with node abstractions in IEC 61970/61968 CIM (e.g., ConnectivityNode and TopologicalNode), while unifying physical and logical coordination entities within a single identity abstraction suitable for graph-based modeling and transactive coordination.

data.Title: linear.one.dimensional.calibration
data.Description:
Linear calibration applied to a measurement expressed in the derived channel's declared OutputUnit domain.
The transformation is interpreted as:

    calibrated = M * x + B

where:

  - x is the input measurement first converted into the OutputUnit

data.Title: report
data.Description: Primary telemetry and state reporting message produced by a SCADA node for a specific reporting slot. A report contains all meaningful channel readings, state transitions, and FSM outputs observed during the slot period.
data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "Reports are sent at fixed slot intervals (typically 5 minutes) and provide a durable historical record of telemetry and state changes observed during that period.
GridWorks SCADA devices emit most channel readings asynchronously when values change beyond configured thresholds. Each reading is timestamped at the moment of observation by the SCADA device. Reports preserve these original timestamps without resampling or aggregation.
As a result, a report represents a batched event log for the slot period rather than a sampled snapshot. Consumers can reconstruct the precise timing of state transitions (e.g., relay changes) and value updates within the slot window.
This differs from snapshot messages, which represent the most recent value of each channel at a single point in time and are optimized for near-real-time visualization rather than historical accuracy.
"}

data.Title: synced.readings
data.Description:

data.Description:

data.RawJson:
{"x-gridworks-extended_description": "
`synced.readings.bundle` represents a rectangular, time-aligned dataset across multiple channels.
ChannelName values are identifiers defined within a GridWorks SCADA layout context (e.g. layout.lite or gw.nolan.layout). They are not globally standardized vocabulary and SHALL be interpreted only within the context in which they were produced.
ChannelDefinitions provides a minimal projection of channel semantics, including `Name`, `Id`, `Unit` and `UnitType`, sufficient to interpret the numeric values in this bundle without requiring access to the full layout.
The `Id` together with the channel TypeName (e.g. `data.channel.gt`, `derived.channel.gt`, or `analytics.channel.gt`) enables resolution of the authoritative channel definition. This bundle is not a source of semantic authority; it provides a convenient projection for transport, indexing, and querying.
In GridWorks systems, full channel definitions are typically available in layout artifacts such as `layout.lite`, which include additional information such as `AboutNodeName`, `CapturedByNodeName`, and derivation strategy.
